```json
{
  "architecture_summary": "EConverter is a self-hosted, single-tenant enterprise document platform built on .NET / ASP.NET Core with a classic Domain-Driven Design layering (Domain, Application, Contracts, Infrastructure, Web, Workers, BuildingBlocks). The runtime is deliberately split into two processes: a Blazor Server + Minimal API web host that owns the user-facing document, editor, Copilot and administration experiences, and a standalone DocumentWorker background service that consumes RabbitMQ job messages and executes the decrypt → verify-hash → convert → upload pipeline. Asynchronous work is modelled as a first-class domain aggregate (ProcessingJob with leases, attempts, progress and a user-safe error taxonomy) rather than being owned by the broker, so RabbitMQ is only a delivery channel while the database remains the authoritative job state — a design that supports the in-process JobProcessorWorker fallback (NoOpQueuePublisher) when no broker is configured. Functionally the system decomposes into nine domains: Document Management, Processing & Conversion, Document Intelligence & AI, PDF Editing & Compression, Storage & Encryption, Identity & Security, Administration & Configuration, Platform Infrastructure, and Presentation & Realtime Interaction. The AI domain is contractually constrained to zero-egress, in-process analysis (IDocumentIntelligenceService) with a local HNSW vector index, while a separate, explicitly-permitted ExternalAiClient handles optional cloud LLM traffic — an intentional two-tier AI posture. Several terminology and structural misalignments exist between documentation and code and are worth flagging: (1) DocumentIntelligenceService is described as belonging to the 'DocumentConverter.Application.AI layer' but physically lives in DocumentConverter.Infrastructure.AI; (2) job execution logic is duplicated across two hosts — the standalone DocumentWorker project and the in-process Web/HostedServices/JobProcessorWorker.cs — meaning 'the processing runtime' is not a single code location; (3) the security building block DocumentConverter.Security (EicarSignatureDetector, ZipBombGuard, FileNameSanitizer) is distinct from Domain/Security (AuditEvent) and Infrastructure/Security (AuditService, ClamAvScanner), so 'the security domain' spans three separate layers with loosely related responsibilities; (4) the DDD 'Contracts' layer is used both for cross-layer DTOs and for message payloads (Contracts/Messages/QueueMessages.cs), blurring application contracts with transport schemas.",
```

```json
"# System Workflow Analysis\n\n**System:** EConverter — self-hosted enterprise document conversion, management and intelligence platform (.NET / ASP.NET Core, DDD layering: Domain, Application, Contracts, Infrastructure, Web, Workers, BuildingBlocks)\n\n**Analysis basis:** Source-code insight summaries + system-context and domain-module research reports. Every workflow below is traced to concrete entry points (`file → method → file`) so it can be validated against the repository.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Main Workflow\n\n- **Workflow Name:** Asynchronous Document Conversion Flow\n- **Importance:** 10.0 — spans 6 domains, is the revenue-facing core capability, and is the only workflow that legitimately crosses the process boundary (web host → RabbitMQ → DocumentWorker).\n- **Description:**\n  A user requests a conversion (single document or tool dialog). The request is validated and persisted as a `ProcessingJob` **aggregate** — the authoritative state holder — and only then published as a transport-level `JobMessage` to RabbitMQ. A background host (either the standalone `DocumentWorker` service or the in-process `JobProcessorWorker`) consumes the message, claims a lease on the job, streams the AES-256-GCM encrypted input from storage to a local temp file, decrypts it chunk-by-chunk with bounded memory, verifies the SHA-256 hash, dispatches to the registered `IDocumentProcessor` for the source/target format pair, then hashes, re-encrypts and uploads the result while appending a `ProcessingJobOutput` reference and transitioning the job to a terminal state. Progress and completion events are pushed to the UI over SignalR.\n\n  **Architectural principle:** RabbitMQ is strictly a *delivery channel*; the database is the *source of truth* for job state. This is what allows the `NoOpQueuePublisher` fallback to degrade gracefully to in-process execution when no broker is configured.\n\n- **Flow Diagram:**\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"Entry: ProcessingEndpoints.cs / Tools/StartConversionDialog.razor\"] --> B[\"IProcessingService.CreateJobAsync\"]\n    B --> C[\"ProcessingService.cs: validate ownership via Security abstractions\"]\n    C --> D[\"ProcessingJob aggregate created in Pending state\"]\n    D --> E[\"ProcessingJobStatus.cs: ProcessingJobLifecycle.EnsureCanTransition\"]\n    E --> F[\"EF Core persist via AppDbContext + ProcessingConfigurations\"]\n    F --> G[\"RabbitMqJobDispatcher: build JobMessage payload\"]\n    G --> H{\"Broker configured?\"}\n    H -->|Yes| I[\"Publish to RabbitMQ exchange\"]\n    H -->|No| J[\"NoOpQueuePublisher fallback\"]\n    I --> K[\"Worker.cs (DocumentWorker) / JobProcessorWorker.cs (Web host)\"]\n    J --> K\n    K --> L[\"ProcessingJob.Claim + RenewLease\"]\n    L --> M[\"Stream P[\"IDocumentProcessor resolved from ConverterCatalogService\"]\n    P --> Q[\"Format-specific processor executes conversion\"]\n    Q --> R[\"Hash + encrypt + upload output to storage\"]\n    R --> V[\"ProcessingJobs.razor / BatchProgressDialog.razor rendered\"]\n```\n\n- **Key Steps:**\n\n| # | Step | Component | Entry Point | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Job creation | Job Orchestration | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Processing/ProcessingService.cs` | Validates request, resolves ownership/security rules, creates `ProcessingJob` in `Pending` |\n| 2 | Lifecycle Converter Catalog | `src/BuildingBlocks/DocumentConverter.Processing.Abstractions/IDocumentProcessor.cs` | Resolves the processor for the source/target format pair |\n| 7 | Conversion | Office/PDF Converters | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Processing/OfficeDocumentProcessor.cs` (+ `Office/ExcelPdfConverter.cs`, presentation, ebook, markdown paths) | Executes the actual format Terminal transition | Aggregates | `src/DocumentConverter.Domain/Processing/ProcessingJob.cs` | `MarkCompleted` / `MarkFailed`, attempts recorded, user-safe error code assigned |\n| 10 | Realtime notification | Presentation | `src/DocumentConverter.Web/Hubs/ProcessingHub.cs` | Pushes progress/completion to the jobs page and batch dialogs |\n\n**Failure semantics:** `ProcessingJobLifecycle.IsRetryable` classifies errors; retryable failures produce a new `ProcessingAttempt` under the same aggregate rather than a new job. The `ProcessingErrorCode` taxonomy is deliberately user-safe and never leaks internal exception detail.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Other Important Workflows\n\n### 2.1 Batch Conversion Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 8.0 — the high-volume, back-office monetization path.\n- **Description:**\n  An operator selects N documents and requests batch conversion. A `BatchJob` aggregate is created and one child `ProcessingJob` per document is generated and linked. Each child is dispatched as an independent `JobMessage`, allowing parallel worker consumption. Batch closure is **not** event-driven — it is recomputed by querying child job states through a scoped `AppDbContext` instance, meaning batch completion is a derived, idempotent aggregate rather than a separately tracked state machine.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"BatchConversionDialog.razor\"] --> B[\"IProcessingService.CreateBatchAsync\"]\n    B --> C[\"BatchJob aggregate created\"]\n    C --> D[\"N child ProcessingJob entities generated + linked\"]\n    D --> E[\"RabbitMqJobDispatcher: one JobMessage per child\"]\n    E --> F[\"Independent workers claim/lease child jobs\"]\n    F --> G[\"Shared single-job conversion pipeline (see 2.1 §1)\"]\n    G --> H[\"JobProcessorWorker queries child states via scoped AppDbContext\"]\n    H --> I{\"All children terminal?\"}\n    I -->|Yes| J[\"Batch marked complete\"]\n    I -->|No| F\n    J --> K[\"BatchProgressDialog.razor + hub notifications\"]\n```\n\n| # | Step | Entry Point | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Batch creation | `src/DocumentConverter.Domain/Processing/BatchJob.cs` | Aggregate + child job fan-out |\n| 2 | Fan-out dispatch | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Messaging/RabbitMqJobDispatcher.cs` | Parallelizable delivery |\n| 3 | Execution | `src/DocumentConverter.Web/HostedServices/JobProcessorWorker.cs` | Reuses single-job pipeline |\n| 4 | Completion aggregation | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Persistence/AppDbContext.cs` | Recompute batch state from child states |\n| 5 | Realtime UI | `src/DocumentConverter.Web/Components/Pages/Documents/Dialogs/BatchProgressDialog.razor` | Aggregated progress display |\n\n---\n\n### 2.2 Document Ingestion & Storage Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 10.0 — every other workflow depends on a persisted `Document`.\n- **Description:**\n  A file is uploaded through the Blazor UI and posted to a minimal-API route. The endpoint resolves caller identity, delegates to the document application service, sanitizes the file name, screens the payload (EICAR signature, zip-bomb ratio, MIME/format verification), re-writes the plaintext stream as a chunked AES-256-GCM envelope with a per-document DEK wrapped by the master KEK, writes it to the storage backend, and finally constructs the `Document` aggregate via its validated `Create` factory. This ordering is deliberate: **no plaintext ever lands in storage, and no aggregate exists before its storage coordinates do.**\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"UploadDialog.razor\"] --> B[\"DocumentEndpoints.cs POST route\"]\n    B --> C[\"Resolve caller identity — ownership context\"]\n    C --> D[\"FileNameSanitizer.cs + EicarSignatureDetector.cs + ZipBombGuard.cs\"]\n    D --> E{\"Screening passed?\"}\n    E -->|No| F[\"Reject — no persistence, audit event\"]\n    E -->|Yes| G[\"AesGcmStorageEncryptionService: chunked AES-256-GCM envelope\"]\n    G --> H[\"Ephemeral DEK wrapped by master KEK\"]\n    H --> I[\"FileSystemDocumentStorage.cs: write envelope\"]\n    I --> J[\"StorageProvider/StorageKey returned\"]\n    J --> K[\"Document.Create factory — owner, hash, size, content type\"]\n    K --> L[\"AppDbContext + DocumentConfigurations persist\"]\n```\n\n| # | Step | Entry Point | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | UI submission | `src/DocumentConverter.Web/Components/Pages/Documents/Dialogs/UploadDialog.razor` | Capture file stream from explorer |\n| 2 | Endpoint routing | `src/DocumentConverter.Web/Endpoints/DocumentEndpoints.cs` | Identity resolution + delegation |\n| 3 | Threat screening | `src/BuildingBlocks/DocumentConverter.Security/FileNameSanitizer.cs` (+ EICAR, ZipBombGuard) | Traversal prevention, malware/expansion defence |\n| 4 | Envelope encryption | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Security/StorageEncryption/AesGcmStorageEncryptionService.cs` | Per-chunk authenticated encryption |\n| 5 | Storage write | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Storage/FileSystemDocumentStorage.cs` | Provider-agnostic persistence |\n| 6 | Aggregate creation | `src/DocumentConverter.Domain/Documents/Document.cs` | Invariant-enforcing factory |\n| 7 | Schema mapping | `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/DocumentConfigurations.cs` | Relational persistence |\n\n**Note:** An optional ClamAV scan (`src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Security/ClamAvScanner.cs`) runs in the same screening stage, with the verdict reported into document lifecycle status (`DocumentStatus` / `BeginScan`).\n\n---\n\n### 2.3 Document Intelligence Indexing Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 9.0 — enables the differentiator (zero-egress semantic search).\n- **Description:**\n  A hosted `DocumentIndexingWorker` pulls pending document references from an `IDocumentIndexingChannel`. The intelligence service enforces access control, loads the encrypted stream, extracts text, applies OCR fallback for scanned PDFs, splits text into overlapping multilingual chunks with language detection, generates embeddings, inserts them into the local HNSW index, and persists `DocumentVectorChunk` / `DocumentIntelligenceIndex` rows so the index survives process restart. All work is in-process — the `IDocumentIntelligenceService` contract forbids content egress.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"DocumentIndexingWorker.cs pulls from IDocumentIndexingChannel\"] --> B[\"DocumentIntelligenceService.cs — access control check\"]\n    B --> C[\"Load + decrypt document stream\"]\n    C --> D[\"Text extraction\"]\n    D --> E{\"ScannedPdfDetector: text layer present?\"}\n    E -->|No| F[\"TesseractOcrEngine.cs OCR fallback\"]\n    E -->|Yes| G[\"MultilingualChunkProcessor.cs — overlap chunking + language detect\"]\n    F --> G\n    G --> H[\"Embedding generation\"]\n    H --> I[\"HnswVectorIndex.cs insertion\"]\n    I --> J[\"Persist DocumentVectorChunk + DocumentIntelligenceIndex\"]\n    J --> K[\"Durable hydration source for next restart\"]\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.4 Grounded Copilot Question-Answering Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 9.0 — the primary user-facing AI surface.\n- **Description:**\n  A user submits a prompt with an active folder/session scope. `EnterpriseAiChatService` resolves or creates the session (maintaining a concurrent in-memory cache), appends the user message, and delegates retrieval to `DocumentIntelligenceService`, which performs HNSW similarity search and ranks candidate chunks **within the caller's scoped folder tree only**. Ranked chunks are assembled into a grounded prompt. If an external provider is explicitly configured, `ExternalAiClient` dispatches the completion; otherwise the in-process path answers. The answer is appended to the `CopilotChatSession` aggregate and persisted.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"AiChatPage.razor / GlobalCopilotDialog.razor — prompt + scope\"] --> B[\"EnterpriseAiChatService.cs — resolve/create session\"]\n    B --> C[\"Append user message to session history\"]\n    C --> D[\"DocumentIntelligenceService.cs — HNSW similarity search\"]\n    D --> E[\"Rank chunks filtered by folder scope\"]\n    E --> F[\"Assemble grounded prompt\"]\n    F --> G{\"External provider configured?\"}\n    G -->|Yes| H[\"ExternalAiClient.cs — provider HTTP dispatch\"]\n    G -->|No| I[\"In-process answer path\"]\n    H --> J[\"Append answer to CopilotChatSession aggregate\"]\n    I --> J\n    J --> K[\"Persist via conversation store\"]\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.5 PDF Editing & Manipulation Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 9.0 — high-value legal/compliance feature set.\n- **Description:**\n  The PDF.js-backed Blazor editor captures user operations, serializes them into `PdfEditOperationDto` payloads, and posts them to `EditorEndpoints`. The server-side `PdfEngine` (stateless) translates each DTO into PDFsharp/PdfPig drawing and document-manipulation calls. Optionally, `PdfCompressProcessor` applies structural compaction plus SkiaSharp image downsampling. The mutated document is re-encrypted, stored, and a new `DocumentVersion` is created so the prior revision is preserved — edits are never destructive.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"PdfEditor.razor + wwwroot/lib/pdfjs/pdfEditor.js — capture ops\"] --> B[\"EditorEndpoints.cs — validate + route batch\"]\n    B --> C[\"PdfEngine.cs — drawing primitives, annotations, forms, page structure\"]\n    C --> D{\"Compression requested?\"}\n    D -->|Yes| E[\"PdfCompressProcessor.cs — stream compaction + SkiaSharp downsampling\"]\n    D -->|No| F[\"Re-encrypt mutated document\"]\n    E --> F\n    F --> G[\"Storage write\"]\n    G --> H[\"DocumentVersion created — prior revision preserved\"]\n```\n\n**Operation coverage:** text rendering, highlights, shapes, ink strokes, image/signature placement, stamps, sticky notes, strikethrough, underline, redaction, watermarking, form fields, page structure. Digital signing is handled by `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Documents/PdfDigitalSignatureService.cs`; glyph consistency by `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/Editor/SystemFontResolver.cs`.\n\n---\n\n### 2.6 Authentication, Authorization & Audit Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 10.0 — gates every other workflow.\n- **Description:**\n  Dual authentication modes: ASP.NET Core Identity (Local) and OIDC federation (Entra ID). Provider claims are transformed into internal application roles via `AppClaimsTransformation`. The `User` aggregate is resolved by normalized email — note that authorization keys on the **internal `Entity.Id`, not the identity-provider subject**, so identity-provider churn cannot leak authorization. `HttpContextUserContext` resolves the current user id for every downstream ownership check. Security-relevant actions are recorded as `AuditEvent` entries.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"Login.razor / AccountEndpoints.cs / Program.cs pipeline\"] --> B{\"Auth mode\"}\n    B -->|Local| C[\"ASP.NET Core Identity — credential + session cookie\"]\n    B -->|EntraId| D[\"OIDC federation — callback\"]\n    C --> E[\"AppClaimsTransformation.cs — map to internal roles\"]\n    D --> E\n    E --> F[\"User aggregate resolved by normalized email\"]\n    F --> G[\"Role membership evaluated via guarded operations\"]\n    G --> H[\"HttpContextUserContext.cs — expose user id\"]\n    H --> I[\"Per-request ownership enforcement in application services\"]\n    I --> J[\"AuditService.cs — record AuditEvent\"]\n    J --> K[\"SecurityAuditLog.razor — admin review\"]\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2.7 Dossier & Report Export Flow\n\n- **Importance:** 8.0 — produces the monetizable end artifact.\n- **Description:**\n  An analyst triggers export of analysis results (financial graph topics, cross-document comparisons, clause diffs, grounded search results). Artifacts are collected and validated against the caller's scope, then materialized by `CopilotDossierExporter` into XLSX workbooks, DOCX reports and Markdown executive briefings using OpenXML. The generated artifact is persisted through the document/storage pipeline as a downloadable document — meaning **exports inherit the same encryption, ownership and versioning guarantees as any other document**.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    A[\"AI export action — Copilot/Analysis UI or API\"] --> B[\"DocumentIntelligenceService.cs — collect + scope-validate artifacts\"]\n    B --> C[\"CopilotDossierExporter.cs — OpenXML XLSX/DOCX + Markdown\"]\n    C --> D[\"DocumentService.cs — persist through storage pipeline\"]\n    D --> E[\"ExportDocumentDialog.razor — download / inline preview\"]\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Workflow Insights\n\n### 3.1 Operational Patterns\n\n- **Database-authoritative async.** Job state lives in the `ProcessingJob` aggregate; RabbitMQ only delivers. This is a deliberate resilience choice — it permits the `NoOpQueuePublisher` broker-less fallback and makes job state recoverable after a broker outage. The cost is that lease/attempt semantics must be enforced in the domain layer rather than relying on broker acknowledgement.\n\n- **Ownership-first authorization.** Every workflow that touches content passes through `Document.IsOwnedBy` / `GetCurrentUserId` before any read or mutation. AI retrieval is additionally filtered by folder scope, so a Copilot session can only ground in documents the caller owns. This is a consistent, single-seam access model.\n\n- **Encryption at the storage boundary.** `AesGcmStorageEncryptionService` is the only place cipher/nonce/tag/key-wrapping logic exists. Because every artifact — uploads, conversions, edits, dossier exports — flows through `IDocumentStorage`, the encryption guarantee is structural rather than per-feature. Per-chunk authentication enables streamed, bounded-memory decryption, which is what makes large-file conversion viable.\n\n- **Two-tier AI posture.** The `IDocumentIntelligenceService` contract mandates zero-egress in-process analysis; `ExternalAiClient` is a separate, explicitly-permitted outbound boundary. This separation is what allows the product to serve regulated/air-gapped deployments while still supporting cloud LLMs when configured.\n\n- **Non-destructive mutation.** Edits create `DocumentVersion` records rather than overwriting; recycle-bin deletion precedes purge. Recoverability is a first-class design property.\n\n- **User-safe error taxonomy.** `ProcessingErrorCode` never leaks internal exception detail — good for security posture, but it means operators must rely on logs/telemetry for root-cause during incidents.\n\n### 3.2 Dependencies Between Workflows\n\n| Upstream Workflow | Downstream Workflow(s) | Dependency Type | Strength |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Document Ingestion & Storage | All conversion, AI, editing, export workflows | Data — no `Document` aggregate, no work | 10.0 |\n| Authentication & Authorization | All workflows (except unauthenticated entry points) | Service Call — ownership gate | 10.0 |\n| Asynchronous Conversion | Batch Conversion | Reuse — batch is N single jobs | 9.0 |\n| Document Ingestion | Intelligence Indexing | Event/queue — indexing channel triggered post-availability | 9.0 |\n| Intelligence Indexing | Grounded Copilot QA | Data — no vectors, no retrieval | 9.5 |\n| Intelligence Retrieval | Dossier Export | Service Call — export consumes ranked artifacts | 8.5 |\n| Document Management | PDF Editing | Service Call — versioned persistence | 9.0 |\n| Storage & Encryption | Every content-bearing workflow | Data / infrastructure | 9.5 |\n| Admin Configuration | Conversion + AI | Configuration — converter availability & AI provider settings | 8.0 |\n\n**Critical path:** Authentication → Document Ingestion → Encryption/Storage → *(fan-out)* Conversion | Indexing → *(fan-in)* Copilot / Dossier Export. Ingestion and encryption are single points of failure for every downstream capability.\n\n### 3.3 Optimization Opportunities\n\n1. **Consolidate duplicated job-execution logic.** Job execution exists in two places — `src/Workers/DocumentWorker/Worker.cs` and `src/DocumentConverter.Web/HostedServices/JobProcessorWorker.cs`. Behavioral drift between the standalone and in-process runtimes is a real risk. Extract the shared pipeline (dequeue → hash-verify → decrypt → convert → upload → complete) into a single implementation consumed by both hosts.\n\n2. **Decompose `DocumentIntelligenceService`.** 5,884 lines / 37 methods / cyclomatic complexity **617** is the highest-risk file in the system and the single entry point for all AI operations. Natural seams: access-control gate, analysis orchestration, embedding generation, HNSW index hydration, similarity ranking, provider configuration persistence. Also note the naming/location mismatch — the research describes it as \"Application.AI layer\" but it physically lives in `Infrastructure/AI`.\n\n3. **Introduce queue backpressure and admission control.** Nothing in the described flow limits concurrent job creation or queue depth. A per-user or per-tenant admission gate (and batch size ceiling) would prevent a single operator from saturating the worker pool.\n\n4. **Make batch completion event-driven or indexed.** `JobProcessorWorker` recomputes batch state by querying child jobs through a scoped `AppDbContext`. At scale this is a polling-and-scan cost proportional to batch size × poll frequency. Either publish per-child completion events that decrement a counter, or add a composite index on `(BatchJobId, Status)`.\n\n5. **Add a lease-expiry reaper.** `RenewLease` exists, but a crashed worker holding a stale lease needs a deterministic reclaim path; otherwise jobs can hang in `Processing` indefinitely.\n\n6. **Unify the security surface.** \"Security\" is spread across three layers with loosely related responsibilities: `BuildingBlocks/DocumentConverter.Security` (EICAR, ZipBombGuard, FileNameSanitizer), `Domain/Security` (AuditEvent), `Infrastructure/Security` (AuditService, ClamAvScanner, StorageEncryption). Consider consolidating the naming so the boundary is discoverable.\n\n7. **Clarify the Contracts layer's dual role.** `Contracts` holds both cross-layer DTOs and transport schemas (`Contracts/Messages/QueueMessages.cs`). Separating application contracts from message payload shapes prevents accidental coupling between API evolution and queue wire format.\n\n8. **Bound the in-memory chat-session cache.** `EnterpriseAiChatService` maintains a concurrent session cache keyed by session id with age-based cleanup. Under many concurrent users this needs a hard cap and eviction policy, not only time-based expiry.\n\n9. **HNSW hydration cost on restart.** Durable index hydration depends on `DocumentVectorChunk` / `DocumentIntelligenceIndex` rows; for large corpora, startup hydration is a cold-start latency source. Consider incremental/lazy hydration or a persisted index snapshot.\n\n### 3.4 Validation Notes — Research vs. Code Reality\n\nThe supplied research reports specifically flag four terminology/structural misalignments that downstream documentation should not propagate as fact:\n\n| # | Reported Statement | Code Reality | Documentation Guidance |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `DocumentIntelligenceService` belongs to the \"DocumentConverter.Application.AI layer\" | Physically located in `src/DocumentConverter.Infrastructure/AI/` | Refer to it as Infrastructure-layer, implementing the Application contract `IDocumentIntelligenceService` |\n| 2 | \"The processing runtime\" as a single location | Logic duplicated across `src/Workers/DocumentWorker/Worker.cs` **and** `src/DocumentConverter.Web/HostedServices/JobProcessorWorker.cs` | Always specify *which* execution host is under discussion |\n| 3 | \"The security domain\" as one module | Spans three layers: `BuildingBlocks/DocumentConverter.Security`, `Domain/Security`, `Infrastructure/Security` | Name the specific layer when documenting security behaviour |\n| 4 | \"Contracts\" layer as a single responsibility | Used for cross-layer DTOs **and** message payloads (`Contracts/Messages/QueueMessages.cs`) | Distinguish application contracts from transport schemas |\n\n**Coverage gaps not fully determinable from the provided materials:** recycle-bin restore/purge as a standalone documented workflow, `DocumentVersion` comparison/diffing end-to-end, and digital-signature verification flow. These exist in the code (referenced via `DocumentService` and `PdfDigitalSignatureService`) but were not enumerated as top-level business flows in the research input.\n\n### 3.5 Cross-Cutting Observation\n\nThe system's coherence comes from a small number of enforced seams: `IUserContext` (who), `IDocumentStorage` + `IStorageEncryptionService` (where and how safely), `ProcessingJob` aggregate + `ProcessingJobLifecycle` (what state is legal), and `IDocumentIntelligenceService` (what may leave the process). Most of the identified risks are not architectural — they are **consolidation and scale** issues sitting on top of an otherwise disciplined design.\n\n---\n\n*Legend for this document: `file` references are repository-relative paths as supplied by the research input. Verification status follows the source reports' confidence scores (system context 0.90, domain modules 8.8/10). Items marked as \"not fully determinable\" require direct repository inspection to confirm.*"
```

```json
      "summary": "The Processing directory is the core domain layer of a document-converter backend, modeling the full lifecycle of asynchronous document conversion jobs (batch jobs, individual jobs, attempts, converters, and job inputs/outputs).       "subdirectory_count": 1,
      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: Infrastructure AI layer of the DocumentConverter backend, responsible for AI-driven document artifacts and asynchronous vector indexing. CopilotDossierExporter.cs generates publication-ready Excel, Word and Markdown executive briefings from enterprise knowledge graphs and dossier requests, while DocumentIndexingChannel.cs provides a bounded Channel-based pipeline that feeds documents into background vector computation. Together they form the AI output/ingestion boundary that bridges contracts, OpenXML serialization and background processing. The AI directory contains the backend application-layer AI capabilities of the DocumentConverter system, centered on a single monolithic DocumentIntelligenceService that handles document analysis, embedding/index hydration, vector similarity ranking, and AI provider configuration. It sits at the intersection of Domain.AI, Contracts.AI, Documents, and Admin, making it the primary hub for all AI-driven document intelligence workflows. Given its backend C# code, very high complexity, and heavy cross-module coupling, it is one of the most business-critical directories in the project. The AI infrastructure directory implements the document converter's local and cloud AI layer: language detection, external provider dispatch (OpenAI/Gemini/Anthropic), and multilingual chunking/translation for vector search. These three files form a cohesive service boundary — detect the document language, route prompt completions to an external provider, and project content bilingually for retrieval. It is core infrastructure consumed directly by the Application layer, so the score is elevated despite the small file count."

      "summary": "The Documents directory contains the core application service layer for the DocumentConverter system, housing the primary document lifecycle service and a PDF digital signature/verification service.       "summary": "The Dialogs directory is the modal dialog component library of the DocumentConverter Blazor Web UI. It contains 14 Radzen-based .razor components that encapsulate document lifecycle operations — upload, rename, move, copy, folder creation, version history, batch conversion, batch progress, PDF digital signing, document diffing, AI intelligence/copilot, and Windows-style properties. Each component is a self-contained UI unit injected with Application-layer services (IDocumentService, IProcessingService, IConverterCatalogService, IPdfDigitalSignatureService, IDocumentIntelligenceService) and communicates back to callers via DialogService close results and NotificationService toasts, so the directory acts as the presentation hub for all document-mutating workflows."

      "subdirectory_count": 0,
      "summary": "This directory contains multiple file groups. Key aspects: This directory is a vendored third-party frontend asset folder (wwwroot/lib/pdfjs) containing the minified Mozilla PDF.js distribution used to render PDF documents in the browser. It is not project-owned business logic; it is a self-contained client-side library consumed by the ASP.NET Core DocumentConverter web application. The pdfjs directory contains the pre-built, minified distribution artifacts of Mozilla's PDF.js library, a pure-JavaScript PDF rendering engine used to parse and display PDF documents in the browser. The files here are third-party vendored library bundles — the main viewer/API bundle plus its companion Web Worker script that performs the heavy parsing and rasterization work off the main thread. They contain no project-specific business logic; their role is purely infrastructural, providing PDF viewing capability to the application. The pdfjs directory contains the client-side PDF.js interactive editing engine for the Document Converter Platform, implemented as a single large IIFE-based browser script. pdfEditor.js exposes a global window.pdfEditor facade that manages document loading, page modeling, annotation/operation stacks (with undo/redo), drag tooling, and .NET interop callbacks, making it a self-contained frontend feature module rather than a shared infrastructure layer."
    },
```
